<title>Notify 3/9: relay APNs pipeline — ES256 JWT, HTTP/2 push, size validation, 410 feedback</title>
<description>
Phase 3 of the <issue id="b95fcd23-95fa-43f6-86a6-81defb9dda77" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-311/e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-custos-apns">MM-311</issue> notification relay. Implementation details: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-17-notification-relay-implementation.md`.

## Scope

Complete the `push` RPC in `crates/notify-relay`:

* **APNs client:** reqwest (workspace 0.13, rustls — ALPN-negotiates h2 against real APNs, h1 against wiremock). Token auth is a **hand-rolled ES256 JWT** over the existing `p256` dep (~30 lines: `{alg, kid}` header + `{iss: team_id, iat}` claims, base64url, ECDSA-sign) — avoids `jsonwebtoken`'s `ring` dependency. Cached, refreshed at 50 min per Apple's 20–60 min rule.
* **Request assembly:** envelope `{"aps": {"alert": {"title": "Custos", "body": "Encrypted notification"}, "mutable-content": 1}, "ezpds": {"v": 1, "kid", "enc", "ct"}}`; headers `apns-topic` (from the handle row — per-handle topics), `apns-push-type`, `apns-priority`, `apns-expiration` (now + ttlSecs). Endpoint overridable via `EZPDS_NOTIFY_APNS_URL` (the wiremock seam, same trick as `EZPDS_PLC_DIRECTORY_URL`).
* **Size validation:** enforce the 4096-byte cap on the fully serialized APNs body server-side (defense in depth against a misbehaving sender) → `tooLarge`.
* **Outcome mapping:** APNs 200 → `delivered`, **410 →** `unregistered` (the pruning back-channel — returned synchronously in the push RPC response), 429/5xx → `apnsError`; per-handle rate bucket (60/h default) → `throttled`.

## Acceptance

* Wiremock-APNs tests: happy path (assert topic/priority/expiration headers + envelope shape), 410 maps to `unregistered`, oversize rejected with a boundary test at exactly 4096 bytes, JWT cached across pushes and refreshed after expiry.
* Loopback e2e: enroll → registerHandle → push → mock APNs receives the request.
</description>

<title>E2E-encrypted notification relay for self-hosted Custos (APNs)</title>
<description>
Implement the notification relay designed in [docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md](<https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/blob/main/docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md>) (design PR <pull-request id="34230e45-6259-4c9a-b58d-6b135adf84e3" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/design-exploration-e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-327f880332d1">malpercio-dev/ezpds#207</pull-request>, **merged** — the doc on `main` is the source of truth and incorporates the review hardening: claim-code enrollment authorization for the official relay, versioned sender keys with re-pin/revocation semantics, explicit v1 replay acceptance, unverified-notice rendering for unauthenticated payloads, per-handle APNs topics, serialized-request padding budget, and the post-reboot keychain window).

## Problem

Self-hosted Custos instances need to deliver push notifications to the official iOS apps (Obsign, admin-companion). APNs auth keys are bundle-ID-bound, so self-hosters cannot push directly — a relay is structurally required. The design makes that relay a **blind courier**: trusted for availability only.

## Architecture (see design doc for full detail)

* **Confidentiality:** payloads HPKE-sealed (RFC 9180, DHKEM-P256 + AES-GCM) to a per-device notification key; decrypted on-device by a Notification Service Extension (`mutable-content: 1`). Neither the relay nor Apple sees plaintext.
* **Integrity:** HPKE Auth mode with pinned, versioned per-instance sender keys — the relay cannot forge authenticated content (it can generate detectable junk pushes and replay; v1 accepts duplicates as benign).
* **Metadata minimization:** opaque push handles bound to the instance's iroh node id (no DIDs/handles/raw tokens at the relay), fixed-size padding budgeted against the serialized APNs request, optional content-free ping mode.
* **Transport:** Custos ↔ relay over iroh, new `ezpds/notify/0` ALPN, reusing the persisted node identity (`iroh_identity`) and `iroh_tunnel.rs` patterns; back-channel carries APNs `410 Unregistered` pruning feedback.
* **Sovereignty:** relay is an open-source workspace crate (`crates/notify-relay/`); any instance points at any relay via `[notifications] relay = "<node id>"`. Official relay requires a claim-code enrollment grant; open enrollment is a config option for self-run relays. Caveat: official bundle IDs require the official relay's APNs key.

## Suggested phasing

1. **Relay crate + Custos sender** — `crates/notify-relay/` (claim-code enrollment grants, handle store with per-handle APNs topic, APNs HTTP/2 client, per-node rate limits, serialized-request size validation with 4 KB boundary test) + `[notifications]` config, device notification-key registration route, versioned sender-key set, sealed-send on first trigger (agent claim pending). Loopback iroh e2e tests with mock APNs.
2. **Wallet NSE** — per-device keypair + shared keychain access group, registration in onboarding, decrypt-and-render extension, unverified-notice fallback + in-app diagnostics.
3. **Admin-companion adoption + operator docs** — ops alert triggers, self-relay runbook, metadata-minimizing ping mode.

## Open questions (from the design doc)

* Enrollment grant distribution for the official relay (ceremony mirrors admin-device pairing)
* Replay hardening beyond v1's accept-duplicates posture (per-device counter + durable replay window)
* Delivery receipts over the iroh back-channel (out of scope v1)
* Android/FCM later (envelope is provider-agnostic)

Not yet scheduled into a wave; split into per-phase issues when picked up.
</description>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

38

477	/// Validate a raw shape into the running configuration, filling defaults.
478	pub fn validate_and_build(raw: RawConfig) -> Result<Config, ConfigError> {
479	    let defaults = RateLimitConfig::default();
480	    let rate_limits = RateLimitConfig {
481	        registrations_per_hour: raw
482	            .rate_limits
483	            .registrations_per_hour
484	            .unwrap_or(defaults.registrations_per_hour),
485	        registrations_burst: raw
486	            .rate_limits
487	            .registrations_burst
488	            .unwrap_or(defaults.registrations_burst),
489	        pushes_per_hour: raw
490	            .rate_limits
491	            .pushes_per_hour
492	            .unwrap_or(defaults.pushes_per_hour),
493	        pushes_burst: raw
494	            .rate_limits
495	            .pushes_burst
496	            .unwrap_or(defaults.pushes_burst),
497	    };
498	    // A bucket with a refill rate but no capacity would reject its very first request,
499	    // which reads as an outage rather than a limit. Disabling is expressed by the rate.
500	    if rate_limits.registrations_per_hour > 0 && rate_limits.registrations_burst == 0 {
501	        return Err(ConfigError::Invalid(
502	            "rate_limits.registrations_burst must be greater than zero unless \
503	             registrations_per_hour is zero (which disables the limiter)"
504	                .into(),
505	        ));
506	    }
507	    if rate_limits.pushes_per_hour > 0 && rate_limits.pushes_burst == 0 {
508	        return Err(ConfigError::Invalid(
509	            "rate_limits.pushes_burst must be greater than zero unless pushes_per_hour \
510	             is zero (which disables the limiter)"
511	                .into(),
512	        ));
513	    }
514	
515	    let apns = ApnsConfig {
516	        key_path: raw.apns.key_path.map(PathBuf::from),
517	        key_id: raw.apns.key_id,
518	        team_id: raw.apns.team_id,
519	        topics: raw.apns.topics.unwrap_or_default(),
520	        sandbox: raw.apns.sandbox.unwrap_or(false),
521	        endpoint: raw.apns.endpoint,
522	    };
523	    // Credentials are all-or-nothing: a half-configured APNs block would bind fine and
524	    // then fail every push, so it's refused at startup instead.
525	    let present = [
526	        apns.key_path.is_some(),
527	        apns.key_id.is_some(),
528	        apns.team_id.is_some(),
529	    ];
530	    if present.iter().any(|p| *p) && !present.iter().all(|p| *p) {
531	        return Err(ConfigError::Invalid(
532	            "apns.key_path, apns.key_id and apns.team_id must be set together".into(),
533	        ));
534	    }
535	
536	    Ok(Config {
537	        database_url: raw
538	            .database_url
539	            .unwrap_or_else(|| "notify-relay.db".to_owned()),
540	        secret_key_path: raw
541	            .secret_key_path
542	            .map(PathBuf::from)
543	            .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("notify-relay-node.key")),
544	        ipv6: raw.ipv6.unwrap_or(true),
545	        open_enrollment: raw.open_enrollment.unwrap_or(false),

547	        rate_limits,
548	    })

553	/// Collect the `EZPDS_NOTIFY_*` slice of the process environment, refusing non-UTF-8
554	/// values rather than panicking on them.
555	pub fn collect_env() -> Result<HashMap<String, String>, ConfigError> {
556	    let mut map = HashMap::new();
557	    for (key_os, val_os) in std::env::vars_os() {
558	        let key = match key_os.to_str() {
559	            Some(k) if k.starts_with("EZPDS_NOTIFY_") => k.to_owned(),
560	            _ => continue,
561	        };
562	        let val = val_os.into_string().map_err(|_| {
563	            ConfigError::Invalid(format!(
564	                "environment variable {key} contains non-UTF-8 data"
565	            ))
566	        })?;
567	        map.insert(key, val);
568	    }
569	    Ok(map)
570	}

686	// Per-node token buckets. In-memory only: a restart forgives everyone, which is the right
687	// trade for a relay whose entire state is re-derivable by re-enrollment — persisting a
688	// limiter would buy an attacker nothing and cost every restart a write amplification.
689	//
690	// The bucket arithmetic is pure (`TokenBucket::take_at`), so exhaustion and refill are
691	// tested against an explicit clock rather than by sleeping.

693	use std::collections::HashMap;
694	use std::sync::Mutex;
695	use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

699	/// A classic token bucket: `capacity` tokens, refilled at `per_second`.
700	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
701	struct TokenBucket {
702	    tokens: f64,
703	    last_refill: Instant,
704	}
705	
706	impl TokenBucket {
707	    fn new(capacity: u32, now: Instant) -> Self {
708	        Self {
709	            tokens: f64::from(capacity),
710	            last_refill: now,
711	        }
712	    }
713	
714	    /// Refill for the elapsed time, then take one token if there is one.
715	    fn take_at(&mut self, capacity: u32, per_second: f64, now: Instant) -> bool {
716	        let elapsed = now
717	            .saturating_duration_since(self.last_refill)
718	            .as_secs_f64();
719	        self.tokens = (self.tokens + elapsed * per_second).min(f64::from(capacity));
720	        self.last_refill = now;
721	        if self.tokens >= 1.0 {
722	            self.tokens -= 1.0;
723	            true
724	        } else {
725	            false
726	        }
727	    }
728	}

730	/// Which budget a request spends from. Registration RPCs and pushes are separate so a
731	/// chatty push load can never lock a node out of dropping a dead handle.
732	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
733	pub enum Bucket {
734	    Registration,
735	    Push,
736	}

738	/// The process-level limiter: one bucket per (node id, bucket kind).
739	#[derive(Debug)]
740	pub struct RateLimiter {
741	    config: RateLimitConfig,
742	    buckets: Mutex<HashMap<(String, Bucket), TokenBucket>>,
743	}
744	
745	/// How long an untouched bucket is kept before the next sweep drops it. Well past a full
746	/// refill at any sane rate, so pruning can never hand back budget.
747	const IDLE_EVICTION: Duration = Duration::from_secs(6 * 3600);
748	
749	/// Prune when the map grows past this, so a flood of one-shot node ids cannot grow it
750	/// without bound between real requests.
751	const PRUNE_THRESHOLD: usize = 1024;
752	
753	impl RateLimiter {
754	    pub fn new(config: RateLimitConfig) -> Self {
755	        Self {
756	            config,
757	            buckets: Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
758	        }
759	    }
760	
761	    /// The (capacity, refill-per-second) pair for a bucket kind. A per-hour rate of zero
762	    /// disables the limiter entirely.
763	    fn limits(&self, bucket: Bucket) -> Option<(u32, f64)> {
764	        let (per_hour, burst) = match bucket {
765	            Bucket::Registration => (
766	                self.config.registrations_per_hour,
767	                self.config.registrations_burst,
768	            ),
769	            Bucket::Push => (self.config.pushes_per_hour, self.config.pushes_burst),
770	        };
771	        if per_hour == 0 {
772	            return None;
773	        }
774	        Some((burst, f64::from(per_hour) / 3600.0))
775	    }
776	
777	    /// Charge one request to `node_id`, returning false when the budget is exhausted.
778	    pub fn check(&self, node_id: &str, bucket: Bucket) -> bool {
779	        self.check_at(node_id, bucket, Instant::now())
780	    }
781	
782	    /// `check` against an explicit clock, so the exhaustion/refill behaviour is testable
783	    /// without sleeping.
784	    pub fn check_at(&self, node_id: &str, bucket: Bucket, now: Instant) -> bool {
785	        let Some((capacity, per_second)) = self.limits(bucket) else {
786	            return true;
787	        };
788	        let mut buckets = self
789	            .buckets
790	            .lock()
791	            .unwrap_or_else(std::sync::PoisonError::into_inner);
792	        if buckets.len() > PRUNE_THRESHOLD {
793	            buckets.retain(|_, b| now.saturating_duration_since(b.last_refill) < IDLE_EVICTION);
794	        }
795	        let entry = buckets
796	            .entry((node_id.to_owned(), bucket))
797	            .or_insert_with(|| TokenBucket::new(capacity, now));
798	        entry.take_at(capacity, per_second, now)
799	    }
800	}

4	// token; the instance sends the handle, never the token, so a compromised relay database
5	// still cannot be correlated with anything an instance said before enrolling.

13	/// A handle row as its owner may see it.
14	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
15	pub struct HandleRow {
16	    pub handle: String,
17	    pub apns_token: String,
18	    pub apns_topic: String,
19	}

21	/// Register (or re-register) a device for `node_id`, returning the live handle.
22	///
23	/// Re-registering the same `(node_id, apns_token)` **rotates** the handle: the old one
24	/// stops resolving in the same transaction the new one starts. Rotation is the point —
25	/// a handle that outlived its registration would be a stale capability.
26	pub async fn register_handle(
27	    db: &SqlitePool,
28	    node_id: &str,
29	    apns_token: &str,
30	    apns_topic: &str,
31	    handle: &str,
32	) -> Result<String, sqlx::Error> {
33	    let mut tx = db.begin().await?;
34	    sqlx::query("DELETE FROM handles WHERE node_id = ? AND apns_token = ?")
35	        .bind(node_id)
36	        .bind(apns_token)
37	        .execute(&mut *tx)
38	        .await?;
39	    sqlx::query(
40	        "INSERT INTO handles (handle, node_id, apns_token, apns_topic, created_at) \
41	         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, datetime('now'))",
42	    )
43	    .bind(handle)
44	    .bind(node_id)
45	    .bind(apns_token)
46	    .bind(apns_topic)
47	    .execute(&mut *tx)
48	    .await?;
49	    tx.commit().await?;
50	    Ok(handle.to_owned())
51	}

53	/// Resolve a handle **owned by** `node_id`. `None` covers both "no such handle" and
54	/// "someone else's handle" — the caller must not distinguish them.

56	    db: &SqlitePool,
57	    node_id: &str,
58	    handle: &str,
59	) -> Result<Option<HandleRow>, sqlx::Error> {
60	    let row = sqlx::query_as::<_, (String, String, String)>(
61	        "SELECT handle, apns_token, apns_topic FROM handles WHERE handle = ? AND node_id = ?",
62	    )
63	    .bind(handle)
64	    .bind(node_id)
65	    .fetch_optional(db)

70	        apns_token,

-- The relay's whole world: who may talk to it, and which opaque handles they own.
--
-- No DIDs, no account handles, no raw device tokens beyond the APNs token Apple itself
-- requires — the relay is a blind courier, and this schema is the limit of what it knows.

-- Enrollment grants, minted by the operator (`notify-relay mint-code`). Status is derived
-- from the timestamps rather than stored (the pds crate's claim_codes doctrine): a code is
-- pending while unconsumed and unexpired, and redemption is a single guarded UPDATE.
CREATE TABLE enrollment_codes (
    code             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at       TEXT NOT NULL,
    expires_at       TEXT NOT NULL,
    consumed_at      TEXT,
    consumed_by_node TEXT
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- Instances allowed to register handles and push. `code_used` is NULL for a node enrolled
-- under open enrollment, which is exactly the audit distinction an operator wants.
CREATE TABLE enrollments (
    node_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    enrolled_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    code_used   TEXT
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- Opaque push handles: 128 bits of randomness standing in for a device's APNs token, so
-- an instance never re-sends the token and the relay never correlates one across nodes.
CREATE TABLE handles (
    handle       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    node_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES enrollments(node_id),
    apns_token   TEXT NOT NULL,
    apns_topic   TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
    last_push_at TEXT
) WITHOUT ROWID;

-- One live handle per (node, token): re-registering the same device rotates the handle
-- rather than accumulating aliases for it.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX handles_node_token ON handles (node_id, apns_token);

-- Every lookup is scoped by the registering node id, so it leads the index.
CREATE INDEX handles_node ON handles (node_id);

# Changelog fragments

Every pull request that changes a shipped surface must add a short Markdown fragment:

```text

==> changelog.d/mm-415.added.md <==
Groundwork for encrypted push notifications: Custos gained the sealing layer that will let a self-hosted instance send notifications through a relay it does not have to trust. Payloads are sealed to a per-device key with HPKE (RFC 9180, DHKEM-P256 + AES-256-GCM, authenticated mode), so a relay operator and Apple both see only opaque bytes and neither can forge a notification your device will accept. Payloads are also padded up to one of three fixed sizes: that does not hide length outright, but it reduces what length can reveal from a per-notification fingerprint to which of three buckets a notification fell into. Nothing is enabled by this change on its own; the relay, the registration flow, and the on-device decryption arrive in the phases that follow.

==> changelog.d/mm-416.added.md <==
New `notify-relay` service: a blind courier that self-hosted Custos instances enroll with over iroh (`ezpds/notify/0`) to obtain opaque push handles for their devices. Enrollment is closed by default and gated on operator-minted single-use codes (`notify-relay mint-code --ttl 60m`); `open_enrollment = true` admits any instance on a self-run relay. Handles are resolvable only by the instance that registered them, and per-instance rate limits apply. Sending pushes to Apple arrives in a following change.

==> changelog.d/mm-456.added.md <==
A recovery key for identities hosted anywhere. Until now, the wallet's Shamir recovery seed came bundled with Custos escrow, so an identity you imported from bsky.social or any other spec-compliant PDS got a Secure-Enclave root key, monitoring, and backups — but no way back in if you lost the device. The new "Add a recovery key" flow on the identity screen is the same ceremony minus the escrow: the wallet generates the seed, splits it 2-of-3, and publishes a device-key-signed operation that inserts the derived recovery key straight after your device key. Nothing is removed, and no share — nor any part of the recovery key — is ever sent to your PDS; the only thing the wallet asks it is the public question of whether it offers recovery escrow at all. Share 1 goes to your Keychain to sync across your Apple devices; Shares 2 and 3 are both yours to save, and any two of the three restore the identity through the existing recovery ceremony. The flow is offered only where it is the right answer: on a server that advertises recovery escrow, the escrow-backed upgrade is offered instead, and on a server that could not be reached nothing is offered at all rather than guessing. If you later move to a host that does hold shares, the wallet offers escrow once — as an option, not a reminder.

==> changelog.d/mm-457.added.md <==
App passwords, handle changes, identity removal, and media restore now work on any server. Four features that are pure standard AT Protocol have been dark for identities hosted anywhere but Custos, for a single reason: each needs a full sign-in, and the only sign-in the wallet knew how to perform was the passwordless one that a Custos server offers. On bsky.social or the reference PDS there was no such option, so the buttons were there and the session behind them was not. The wallet now asks the identity's server which sign-in it supports and offers the right one: a Face ID unlock where the server accepts a device-key signature, and a prompt for your account password where it does not — with emailed two-factor codes handled, and the password sent once, to your own server, and never stored. From then on the session behaves identically either way: it refreshes on its own, and it is discarded if your identity moves to a different host. A server the wallet could not reach is never assumed to lack passwordless sign-in — it keeps offering the unlock it already used, because a network hiccup is not a fact about your server.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Require a changelog fragment *added by the change itself* when a PR changes a shipped
# surface (fragments already sitting in changelog.d/ from other work don't satisfy it).
# CHANGELOG_BASE_REF is set to the PR base SHA in CI; an explicit first argument is
# convenient for local checks. With neither, fragment validity is still checked but
# presence is not required because there is no trustworthy comparison range.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

base_ref="${1:-${CHANGELOG_BASE_REF:-}}"
fragment_dir="changelog.d"
fragment_re='^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\.(added|changed|fixed|removed|security)\.md$'

fail=0
fragment_count=0
while IFS= read -r fragment; do
  name="${fragment##*/}"
  if ! [[ "$name" =~ $fragment_re ]]; then
    echo "✗ invalid changelog fragment '$fragment' — expected <id>.<added|changed|fixed|removed|security>.md" >&2
    fail=1
    continue
  fi
  if ! grep -q '[^[:space:]]' "$fragment"; then
    echo "✗ changelog fragment '$fragment' is empty" >&2
    fail=1
    continue
  fi
  fragment_count=$((fragment_count + 1))
done < <(find "$fragment_dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' ! -name README.md | sort)

if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$base_ref" ]; then
  echo "✓ $fragment_count valid changelog fragment(s); no base ref supplied, so presence was not evaluated"
  exit 0
fi

questions.question: When APNs answers 410 Unregistered, should the relay delete its own handle row, or keep it and only report `unregistered` back to the instance?

options.label: Report only, keep the row (Recommended)
options.description: The relay answers `unregistered` and leaves the handle intact. The instance deletes its registration and stops pushing; the row ages out when the device re-registers (which rotates it) or the instance calls dropHandle. Keeps the response idempotent — a lost RPC response means a retry still says `unregistered` rather than the ambiguous `unknownHandle`.

options.label: Delete the row too
options.description: The relay prunes eagerly, so a dead token can never be pushed to twice and the relay stops storing a token Apple has disowned. Cost: a retried push after a lost response answers `unknownHandle`, which reads to the instance as 'someone else's handle' rather than 'this device is gone'.

options.label: Delete, but keep a tombstone
options.description: Mark the row unregistered (a timestamp column) rather than deleting, so retries still answer `unregistered` and the token stops being usable. Costs a V002 migration and a nullable column this phase otherwise doesn't need.

questions.question: A push carries an optional `ttlSecs`. What should `apns-expiration` be when the sender omits it?

options.label: 1 hour (Recommended)
options.description: now + 3600. A notification banner an hour stale is worthless anyway, and Apple will hold it for a device that is briefly offline (commute, overnight airplane mode) instead of dropping it.

options.label: Immediate (expiration 0)
options.description: Apple attempts delivery once and discards on failure. Most privacy-preserving — nothing queues at Apple — but a phone that is off for two minutes silently misses the notification.

options.label: 24 hours
options.description: now + 86400. Maximises delivery, but a day-old 'agent claim pending' banner arriving after the claim already expired is actively misleading.
